omissions:
This plan is an abridgement, and the honest account of an abridgement is what it
leaves out. All figures below are verse counts taken from the Douay-Rheims
(Challoner) text indexed in this repository, whose 73 books hold 35,804 verses.
Percentages computed on a 66-book canon run higher for every class named here,
because the denominator is smaller; the commonly quoted figures of about 19.8 per
cent for the prophets, 14.4 per cent for wisdom and poetry and 8.1 per cent for
the epistles are of that kind.

At its fullest tier this plan reads 13,867 verses, 38.7 per cent of the Bible.
The narrative tier reads 3,675 verses, 10.3 per cent. The overview tier reads
1,210 verses, 3.4 per cent.

The reduction does not come from cutting genealogies and law codes. Those are
small: every genealogy and register dropped here comes to 297 verses, 0.8 per
cent of the Bible, and the whole of Leviticus, Exodus 25-31 and 35-40, Numbers
1-9 and 26-30 and Deuteronomy 12-26 together come to 2,217 verses, 6.2 per cent.
Seven per cent, between them. The reduction comes from dropping three whole
classes of book that are not narrative, which come to 15,519 verses, 43.3 per
cent of the Bible.

Not read at any tier:

  The prophets, 5,875 verses, 16.4 per cent of the Bible (counting Lamentations,
  Baruch and Daniel among them). What survives is fifteen passages in thirteen
  readings, and the narrative chapters of Daniel: Isaias 7:1-17, 9:1-7, 11:1-10,
  52:13-53:12, 54:5-14 and 55:1-11; Jeremias 31:31-40, 36 and 38:1-13; Baruch
  3:9-15 with 3:32-4:4; Ezechiel 34, 36:16-28 and 37:1-14; Lamentations 3:19-33;
  Daniel 1-6, 13 and 14. Everything else is absent - the whole of Osee through
  Malachias, all but six passages of Isaias, all but three of Jeremias, Daniel's
  visions, and every oracle against the nations. A reader who finishes this plan
  has not read the prophets.

  The wisdom and poetical books, 6,881 verses, 19.2 per cent. Job, Proverbs,
  Ecclesiastes, the Canticle of Canticles, Wisdom and Ecclesiasticus are not read
  at all. Of the 150 psalms, sixteen are read, each because a narrative moment
  demands it.

  The epistles, 2,763 verses, 7.7 per cent. All twenty-one, and Hebrews with
  them. The plan follows the Church's expansion through the Acts and stops; it
  does not read what the apostles wrote to the churches they founded. That is the
  largest gap in its New Testament coverage, and no narrative plan can close it,
  because the epistles are not narrative.

  The Apocalypse, but for 21:1-22:5, read as the close of the arc opened in
  Genesis 1.

Also not read, being narrative or historical but doubled, legal, or list:
Leviticus entire; Exodus 25-31 and 35-40; Numbers 1-9 and 26-30 apart from
chapter 27; Deuteronomy 12-26; Josue 12-22; Judges 17-21; 1 and 2 Paralipomenon
entire, as a second telling of reigns already read in Samuel and Kings; Aggeus,
Zacharias and Malachias, though they belong to the Return; and 2 Machabees but
for chapters 6 and 7.

Genealogies and registers dropped: Genesis 5, 10, 22:20-24, 25:12-18 and 36;
Exodus 6:14-30; Esdras 2; Nehemias 3 and 7. Genesis 11:10-32 and St. Matthew 1
are kept, because they are the two genealogies that carry the plot.

The consensus narrative spine within the twelve periods is 334 chapters. This
plan reads 331 of them, holding back only Esdras 2, Nehemias 3 and Nehemias 7,
and adds the material listed at the year tier. It touches 454 chapters in 31 of
the 73 books.

The cost is stated here because every abridgement that concealed it has been
attacked for concealing it. A reader who wants the Bible should read the Bible.
What this offers is the story in order, at three depths, with the seams visible.

periods.summary: The Acts of the Apostles entire, from the Ascension to Rome, with three psalms the apostles preach from, and one passage of the Apocalypse to close the arc opened in Genesis 1. The epistles are not read; see the omissions.

plan: The Narrative Spine: an abridged reading of salvation history

narrative.description: The story told continuously: 111 readings, the 36 above plus 75 more, at 3,675 verses or 10.3 per cent of the Bible. Adds the connecting episodes, so that cause and consequence hold from Genesis 12 to Acts 28. Confined to the consensus narrative spine, and to it alone: at this tier the plan reads no prophet, no psalm, no gospel but St. Luke, and none of the narrative deuterocanon but 1 Machabees.
narrative.label: Narrative

overview.description:
Thirty-six sittings, two to four in each period: the hinge readings, without which the arc does not stand. 1,210 verses, 3.4 per cent of the Bible. It is deliberately jumpy - a skeleton, not yet a story.

The three tiers nest. Every reading carries the tier at which it first appears, and no reading appears twice, so a tier is read by taking every reading marked at that tier or above, in order. The lower tiers therefore fill the gaps between the higher ones rather than restating them, and no passage is read twice in one pass.
overview.label: Overview

year.description: The full spine at about a chapter to a reading: 357 readings, 13,867 verses, 38.7 per cent of the Bible, touching 454 chapters in 31 books. Adds to the narrative tier the three remaining gospels where they give what St. Luke does not; the narrative deuterocanon - Daniel, Esther, Tobias, Judith and 2 Machabees 6-7; and the non-narrative passages the story is unintelligible without: the messianic prophecies of Isaias, the new covenant of Jeremias, the shepherd and the dry bones of Ezechiel, and sixteen psalms. At roughly a reading a day it runs a year with eight days to spare.
